title: Order of volatility
scenario: A compromised host has been isolated from the network and is still running. Legal wants a full forensic investigation. Place these evidence sources in the order they should be collected.

items.label: RAM: running processes and network connections
Logs held on a remote server

subtasks.label: CPU registers and cache first
subtasks.correctNote: Gone in nanoseconds. First or not at all.

subtasks.label: RAM second
subtasks.correctNote: Memory holds the running malware, injected code and live connections, and it dies with the power. This is why the host was isolated rather than switched off.

subtasks.label: Temporary files and swap third
subtasks.correctNote: Survives until a reboot or a cleanup job.

subtasks.label: Disk fourth
subtasks.correctNote: Persistent. It will still be there in an hour, which is exactly why it is not first.

subtasks.label: Remote logs fifth
subtasks.correctNote: Held off the host, so the host's fate does not touch them.

subtasks.label: Archives and backups last
subtasks.correctNote: The most durable evidence there is.
